extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students studying commutative algebra (modules, flatness, localization, Tor)
extracted.subtask_description: Solutions and worked facts about modules: direct sums and limits, flatness and Tor, tensor products, polynomial rings, localization, and characterizations of absolutely flat rings. The page gives statements, necessary-and-sufficient conditions, and proof sketches for these properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of map between direct sums and componentwise characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: If M = ⊕_{i∈I} Mi and N = ⊕_{i∈I} Ni and fi : Mi → Ni are module maps, then there exists f : M → N with π_{N,j} ◦ f ◦ ι_{M,i} = fi if i = j and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moreover f is injective (resp. surjective) iff every fi is injective (resp. surjective). The construction follows from the universal property of direct sums and checking components via projections and inclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct sum flatness criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct sum M = ⊕_{i} Mi is flat as an A-module iff each component Mi is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces flatness to injectivity of j ⊗ 1 for arbitrary injective j, then applies the componentwise map claim to deduce equivalence with all component maps being injective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free modules are flat
rubrics_metrics.description: Every free A-module is a flat A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A free module is a direct sum of copies of A, and tensoring with A is exact (A ⊗_A M ≅ M), so direct sums of copies of A are flat (use direct-sum flatness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial ring A[x] is flat as A-module
rubrics_metrics.description: As an A-module, A[x] ≅ ⊕_{i∈ℕ} (xi) and each (xi) ≅ A, so A[x] is flat over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit explicit isomorphism sending polynomial to tuple of coefficients; use that each summand is free and apply the direct-sum flatness result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial ring over integral domain is integral domain
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an integral domain then A[x] is an integral domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use degree argument: if f nonzero is a zero divisor then af = 0 for some a ≠ 0, which contradicts degree behaviour in an integral domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of flat modules is flat
rubrics_metrics.description: If M and N are flat A-modules then M ⊗_A N is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exactness of tensoring by each flat module and the associativity/properties of tensor product; use Proposition 2.15 style long exact sequence arguments in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness under change of scalars (transitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a flat A-algebra (flat as an A-module) and N is flat as a B-module, then N is flat as an A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View the maps j ⊗ 1 as B-module maps and use that N is flat over B and B is flat over A; compose isomorphisms and injective maps to conclude injectivity for the A-module tensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation extension criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If M' ⊆ M and M' and M/M' are finitely generated then M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lift generators of the quotient to M and combine with generators of the submodule to produce a finite generating set of M; use the correspondence between submodules containing M' and submodules of M/M'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity detected mod an ideal (Nakayama-type lifting)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a map M → N induces a surjection modulo an ideal a (i.e., u(M) + aN = N) and the hypotheses of Corollary 2.7 apply, then u(M) = N (hence u is surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the given corollary / Nakayama-type argument: surjectivity modulo a together with the ideal being in the Jacobson radical forces surjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank comparison for free modules and localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If A^m ≅ A^n as A-modules then m = n. If a surjective map A^m → A^n exists then n ≤ m. If an injective map A^m → A^n exists with m > n leads to contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tensor with residue field k = A/m to obtain k^m ≅ k^n and compare vector space dimensions; use exact sequences and Proposition 2.4 style arguments for injectivity contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting lemma for modules (retraction implies direct sum)
rubrics_metrics.description: If r : M → N and s : N → M satisfy r ◦ s = id_N then M ≅ N ⊕ coker(s) ≅ N ⊕ ker(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct explicit isomorphism φ(m) = (r(m), class_of_m) and inverse maps; show ker and coker correspond via a provided map ψ. Standard splitting lemma proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of free summand from surjection onto A^n and finite generation of kernel
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ : M → A^n is surjective and e_i basis of A^n, choose preimages u_i; the submodule N generated by the u_i is free of rank n and M ≅ N ⊕ ker(φ), with ker(φ) finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the splitting lemma with r = φ and s given by chosen preimages; finite generation of kernel follows from quotient being finitely generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor embedding splits for base extension
rubrics_metrics.description: For g : N → N⊗_A B given by n ↦ 1⊗n, g is injective and g(N) is a direct summand of N⊗_A B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define p(b⊗y)=by as a left inverse: p∘g = id_N. Use the splitting lemma to deduce direct-summand property of g(N).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit universal property and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Given directed system (Mi, µ_{ij}), any family of compatible maps α_i : Mi → N induces a unique α : lim→ Mi → N with α ◦ µ_i = α_i. The direct limit is unique up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the induced map via universal property; uniqueness follows by applying the universal property to both candidate limits and comparing maps (standard categorical argument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modules are directed unions of finitely generated submodules (direct limit description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any module M is the direct limit of its directed system of finitely generated submodules; concretely M = lim→ Mi where Mi run over finitely generated submodules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each element x pick Ax generated by x; finite sums of such submodules form a directed set. Use uniqueness of direct limits to identify the direct limit with M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness preserved by direct limits (colimits are exact on directed systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → M → N → P → 0 is an exact sequence of directed systems, then the induced sequence of direct limits is exact: Im(limit map) = ker(limit map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the universal property and element-wise representatives from components to lift kernels to images; the proof exhibits representatives µ_i(m_i) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product commutes with direct limits
rubrics_metrics.description: (lim→ Mi) ⊗_A N ≅ lim→ (Mi ⊗_A N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the canonical bilinear maps gi : Mi × N → Mi ⊗ N and use universal properties of tensor and direct limits to produce mutually inverse maps between the two constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit of rings/algebras inherits ring/A-algebra structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct limit A = lim→ Ai of rings has a ring structure defined compatibly via maps α_i, with α_i multiplicative and preserving 1; similarly direct limits of A-algebras inherit A-action well-definedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define product using a common index k ≥ i,j and check independence of choices via directedness and eventual equality in further indices; verify axioms componentwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilradical and integral domain behaviour under direct limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If each Ai is an integral domain then A = lim→ Ai is an integral domain. The nilradical of A is the direct limit of the nilradicals of Ai; nilpotent elements lift from some component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representatives α_i(xi) and Proposition 2.15 style pointwise lifting to show if a product is zero then some further component product is zero and deduce contradictions when components are domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing Tor theorem and flatness characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Tor_A^n can be computed from a projective (or free) resolution of either argument (balancing theorem). In particular, M is flat iff Tor_A^n(M, N) = 0 for all n > 0 and all N (equivalently Tor_1(M, N)=0 for all N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use free/projective resolutions and exactness preserved under tensoring by a flat module; the balancing theorem allows checking Tor vanishing from either variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness detected by Tor with quotient modules A/a
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module N is flat iff Tor_1^A(A/a, N) = 0 for all finitely generated ideals a of A (equivalently check Tor_1 with modules A/a arising from finitely generated ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by induction on generators of a finitely generated M using short exact sequences 0 → Mi−1 → Mi → A/ai → 0 and long exact sequences of Tor to propagate vanishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of absolutely flat rings (von Neumann regular / absolutely flat)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are equivalent (sketch in text): (i) every A-module is flat (A is absolutely flat); (ii) every principal ideal (x) satisfies (x) = (x)^2 (idempotent principal ideals); (iii) every finitely generated ideal is principal and generated by an idempotent, hence is a direct summand of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use tensoring the short exact sequence 0→(x)→A→A/(x)→0 and Nakayama-type arguments to deduce idempotence; conversely idempotent generation yields splitting and hence flatness of all modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and examples of absolute flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean rings and rings where each x satisfies x = x^n (for some n depending on x) are absolutely flat. A local absolutely flat ring must be a field. In an absolutely flat ring, every nonunit is a zero divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the idempotent/principal ideal characterization to derive these properties; example arguments shown in text (e.g., local case forces idempotents to be 0 or 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-definedness of localization S^{-1}A
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring of fractions S^{-1}A (elements a/s) is well-defined: addition and multiplication are independent of representatives and S^{-1}A is a commutative ring with identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show equivalence relation on pairs (a,s) via existence of u∈S with (as' - a's)u = 0; verify operations respect representatives and standard ring axioms hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization commutes with tensor product
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a unique isomorphism of S^{-1}A-modules f : S^{-1}M ⊗_{S^{-1}A} S^{-1}N ≅ S^{-1}(M ⊗_A N) with f((m/s)⊗(n/t)) = (m⊗n)/(st). In particular, (M⊗_A N)_p ≅ M_p ⊗_{A_p} N_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct maps through repeated uses of properties of localization and tensor product, checking the canonical images of simple tensors and using previous propositions about tensoring and localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity is a local property
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module homomorphism φ : M → N is surjective iff for every prime (or every maximal) ideal p, the localized map φ_p : M_p → N_p is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If φ surjective then localizations are surjective. Conversely, if φ_p surjective for all maximal p, consider cokernel and use that vanishing of its localizations implies cokernel = 0 (Proposition 3.8 style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction criterion for ideals under localization
rubrics_metrics.description: For f : A → S^{-1}A the contraction a = f^{-1}(f(a)) equals a iff no element of S is a zero divisor in A/a. Equivalently, a is contracted ⇔ whenever s x ∈ a for s∈S then x∈a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characterization of contracted ideals via annihilation by elements of S and relate to zero-divisors in A/a. Also S^{-1}r(a) = r(S^{-1}a) holds (radical commutes suitably with localization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated module annihilation and localization-zero criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For finitely generated M, S^{-1}M = 0 iff there exists s∈S that annihilates M (sM = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If S^{-1}M = 0 then each generator becomes 0 after multiplying by some s_i; take product; conversely if sM = 0 then all localized elements vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units in S^{-1}A for S = 1 + a (partial criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S = 1 + a for an ideal a, then an element a/s ∈ S^{-1}a is such that 1 - (a/s)(x/t) is a unit in S^{-1}A under the computations indicated (use 1 − ax/(1+b) formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text sketches the verification using representative manipulations in S^{-1}A and Proposition 1.9 style unit tests; full detail continues beyond the chunk shown.
